text: Designing for multi-tenancy — three models for how much of the stack your tenants actually share, and what each one costs you.

Shared means one schema for everyone, tagged by tenant_id — cheap, but the weakest isolation. Siloed means one database or workspace per tenant — strong isolation, more infrastructure. Hybrid pools most tenants and siloes the large or regulated ones.

Adding a tenant_id column is the easy part. One missed filter in one report leaks tenant A's rows to tenant B. Real enforcement lives in a security predicate on the table itself, so no query can skip it — not application code that has to remember.

Fabric Capacities make this concrete: one workspace's runaway query can throttle every other workspace sharing that capacity. That's the noisy-neighbor problem, and it's exactly why the largest or most demanding tenants tend to end up siloed.
The model isn't a house style — it's decided against the actual non-functional requirement, tenant by tenant. Next up: designing for data freshness SLAs.
